cohort: The study included 200 singleton pregnancies at >=28 weeks gestation, categorized into groups based on AFI (<5 cm and >5 cm).
finding: Low AFI (<5 cm) in the third trimester is significantly associated with higher rates of adverse perinatal outcomes, including cesarean delivery, fetal distress, meconium-stained fluid, NICU admission, and lower birth weight, independent of maternal risk factors.
mod_finding: The group with AFI <5 cm showed significantly higher rates of cesarean delivery (60%) compared to the group with AFI >5 cm.
birth_weight: N/A (measured as an outcome, not an inclusion criterion)
